text: Chris, are you all right?
Uh-huh.
Huh?
Ah, I feel marvellous.
Good, good. It'll pass. You're fit.
What about him?
He doesn't look too good, I'm afraid.
What did you find out?
Not much. Not enough to locate Skagra. Just enough to frighten me out of my wits.
Chris?
Yes?
Still feeling marvellous?
Yes.
Good. Distracted. Give me ten seconds.
Uh, uh, wait. Well, uh, come on then. Come on. Come on then.
I know, K-9. I know.
It's going for the equipment, Doctor.
K-9. Caldera, wake up, man. Professor Caldera.
Oh, no.
Chris, jump. K-9, outside now.
Down here. Come on. Come on. In here.
I should have been able to save them.
But they were dead.
We don't know that. I only checked on Caldera. The others might have been...
Master, I only detected two viable humanoid lifeforms in that room.
Yourself and Christopher Parsons.
I see. Thank you, K-9.
K-9. Let's get out of here.
Emergency. Emergency.
Imminent explosion in our facility.
Emergency escape procedures will be initiated.
Think tank station's emergency systems are damaged.
Damaged by the stupid creature you created, ship.
The Krag's metabolism has reacted with the power systems of the think tank station.
Destruction imminent. We should depart immediately.
Yes, well, just stop nattering and get on with it.
Stop!
That's the way I told you how to do it. Dematerialize.
All those brilliant minds. Gone forever.
Well done, ship. You're learning. Which is more than we're doing.
What do you mean?
We're still no nearer finding Skagra.
What do you think we should do?
I don't know.
Well, try looking on the bright side.
I have. There's nothing there. Now listen to me, ship.
I hear you.
Good. Now I'm going to ask you once again. Where is your Lord Skagra?
He did not reveal his destination to me.
But you must have some idea.
I am a computer. I do not have ideas. I obey instructions.
So you've no idea where he's gone?
I do not.
Well, doesn't the wretched man have a home to go to?
Yes.
He has?
Yes.
Then why didn't you tell me?
You didn't ask.
Ugh. Will you please take us there?
Doctor, much of my circuitry feels uneasy about continuing to accept instructions from a dead man.
Yes, well, just tell it not to.
I'm sure your Lord Skagra will be very anxious to pay his last respects to me.
Instructions accepted.
Computers. They're so literal-minded, aren't they, K-9?
Master!
Look, Professor. I don't even know what I'm meant to be doing.
We must get this old TARDIS of mine moving again.
Well, it certainly moved when I touched it.
A spasm. A mere spasm. I only hope it wasn't a dying spasm.
Because it has left us jammed between two irrational time interfaces. And time is moving away from us.
I see.
If we ever do manage to disentangle ourselves, I'll have to be careful, otherwise I shall cease to exist again.
Oh, really?
Now, do as I do.
What's that?
Forget about it.
That's easier said than done. Who is this Salyevin person?
Salyevin is, or was, a criminal of sorts. The stories of his exploits have been wildly exaggerated.
He was just a hot-headed, brilliant young man with rather a peculiar talent.
Botheration?
I can't fix this.
Can I help?
It's difficult. It's very difficult.
To repair an interfacial resonator requires two operations which must be performed absolutely simultaneously.
And to be honest, my dear, I don't think you have the knowledge.
So we're stuck?
Yes.
I could learn, you know. I'm very quick.
What's the matter?
Listen to me. Listen to me very carefully.
What I am about to do, you are never to speak of.
And this is the only time I will ever do it.
What are you talking about?
Do I have your promise?
Well, what are you going to do?
Do I have your promise?
Yes, yes, all right.
What is that piece of equipment you are holding in your hand?
I have absolutely no idea.
Good. Now close your eyes and let your mind relax.
Go blank.
Open your eyes. What is that piece of equipment?
This? It's a conceptual geometry relay with an agronomic trigger.
And a totally defunct field separator.
But it doesn't really matter.
We can dispense with it if we can get that interfacial resonator working again.
Splendid.
Well, let's do it then, shall we?
Well? Well what?
Shh! Report!
Your ship has docked with us, my lord.
My ship? What is it doing here?
Perhaps it missed your company.
We should prepare for all eventualities.
How is the work in the vats proceeding?
We have a full complement of Krags, my lord.
Created to my specifications?
They have rudimentary movement and understanding of basic commands.
Good. Then let us go.
Why do you need this army of witless thugs, Skagra?
They have an important part to play later in my...
Doctor.
Oh, hello there.
Doctor, how did you get here?
These kind people brought me.
Krags. Oh, Doctor.
Hello, Chris.
Romana?
Oh, canine. How are you?
Fully recharged, mistress.
Enough of these pleasantries.
Doctor, I am a little surprised to find you here.
Your ship was a little surprised to find itself bringing me.
You stole my ship?
Only after you stole mine.
Oh, there she is.
I hope you've been looking after her. May I check if you've been over-revving her in third phase?
You will not pass without Lord Skagra's permission.
I'm curious to know how you survived the treatment of my sphere.
It only looks for what it expects to find. I made it look for the wrong things. We Time Lords have very slippery minds.
So I am aware, Doctor. If you have come here in the hope of interfering with my great purpose, I'm afraid you will be...
Great purpose? Ha!
Yes, Doctor. The very greatest.
I know what you want to do. You want to take over the universe, don't you? I've met your sort before.
Any moment a mad gleam will come into your eye, you'll start shouting, the universe will be mine!
How naive, Doctor. How pathetically limited your vision.
Limited?
Take over the universe? Oh, how childish. Who could possibly want to take over the universe?
Exactly. This is what I keep trying to tell people. It's a troublesome place. Difficult to administer.
And as a piece of real estate, it's worthless. Because by definition, there'd be nobody to sell it to.
Such visions are for infants. My purpose is to fulfill the natural evolutionary goal of all life.
Oh, yes.
With the aid of the sphere, I shall make the whole of creation merge into one single mind. One god-like entity.
You will?
The universe, Doctor, shall not, as you so crudely put it, be mine. The universe shall be me.
Have you discussed this with anybody? Why don't you send one of your crogs to make some tea and we can sit down?
Doctor, your inane witterings do not interest me. This will happen. It will start within hours. At once started, nothing you or anyone can do will stop it.
Commander, take them away, lock them up, melt down the key.
Canine, now!
Romana, Chris, run!
No, you don't, Romana!
Get off me!
Canine, go!
Tell the Doctor!
Be silent!
Clans, get after them! Kill them!
Clever feint, don't you think? Making him think I was trying to get to the TARDIS.
What were you trying to do?
Get to the TARDIS.
Where are we?
Lost.
What now, Canine?
The Mistress. She is not with us.
Oh, Romana. Never mind, she'll be fine. Keep moving. Down here.
Fools! This is my command ship. Where do they think they can go? They will be caught and destroyed.
What do you have done with this one, my lord?
Romana will come with us to Sharda.
Sharda?
Yes. Enough time has been taken. We will leave now. In your TARDIS.
Come on!
Doctor, that man must be mad, mustn't he?
Madness, sanity, it's all just a matter of opinion.
What's your opinion?
He must be mad. And infinitely dangerous.
You mean he's serious? He can do all that?
It's possible.
Master, Krog's approaching.
In here. Quickly. Now stay quiet. Back the way we came. Quietly.
What?
That.
I'm surprised we can hear it from here.
There's something odd about it.
Come on. Around here. This wasn't here before.
Master, this doorway is inconsistent with the other doorways aboard this ship.
You mean because it's made of wood, not metal?
And because this little nameplate says Chronotis Professor J.F. How interesting.
Master, the creatures have spotted us and are converging on this area.
K-9, how I've missed having you round to tell me the pigmily of...
What do we do now?
Now? We go through this door.
Get in.
It's clear.
Doctor! Professor!
Cup of tea?
Those monsters will burn their way through the door if they don't knock it down first.
Oh, I doubt it, my boy. Hello again, Doctor. How do you like my tardis?
I never realized.
It's strictly unofficial. I'm not really allowed to have one.
There's a much better way to hide it than by living in it, you old sly boots.
Chris! What are you doing here?
How am I supposed to know?
I know this may sound odd, but have you seen my bike at all? Only I lent it to the doctor.
Your bike? No. What's the professor's room doing here?
Oh, you may well ask. But ask the professor.
Doctor, where is Skagra?
Probably going somewhere in my tardis. He's got my tardis, you see, and he's got Romana, and he's got the book.
I thought you were dead, Professor.
Yes, so did I. Now listen, Doctor. If Skagra has the tardis and the book, he can get to Sharda.
Sharda? Sharda?
Yes, the Time Lord's prison planet. You've probably forgotten about it.
I never forget anything. I never...
That's right, I had forgotten. The Time Lord's prison planet. Now, why would I have forgotten that?
Well, of course, Salyavian was imprisoned on Sharda. Claire, ask me who Salyavian was.
Oh, he was a great criminal imprisoned centuries ago by the Time Lords.
Oh, yes. Well, a great criminal, unique mental powers. He had the capacity to project his mind into other minds, didn't he, Professor?
And that's what Skagra's doing.
No, no, no. With Skagra, it's quite the opposite. Skagra has the capacity to take minds out of people.
But he can't put minds into them. This is why he needs Salyavian in his sphere, and that's why he's going to Sharda.
Of course!
Doctor, he must not get there.
Well, obviously, Professor. I mean, with Skagra's mind and Salyavian's mind in the sphere, Skagra will become omnipotent.
Well, do you mean he could just move himself into every mind in the universe?
Oh, yes, eventually. It might take thousands of years, but that wouldn't matter. His mind would be immortal. It would spread like a disease.
That's quite a thought, though, isn't it? Every mind working together as a single organism. A single mind.
Skagra's mind. Not a pleasant thought.
Doctor, we've got to stop him from getting to Sharda.
Yes, but how? He's got a start on us and we don't know the way.
We must follow him.
But how?
The same way we arrived.
You've followed the TARDIS's space time trail. Of course. Then let's get moving.
Yes.
Sharda. The book worked, Romana. It programmed your TARDIS and brought us here. The key turns slowly in the lock. The door to Sharda opens.
Beware.
This is the prison planet, Sharda. Unauthorized entry is punishable by matter dispersion. Unauthorized entry is punishable by matter dispersion. There is no authorized entry.
It looks utterly dismal.
It was built by your race. A prison planet.
Did you hear the warning?
What of it?
Matter dispersion? I don't like the sound of that.
Commander, keep her silent.
Yes, my lord, silent.
Absolutely. Anything you say.
Ah, excellent. This antediluvian technology still functions perfectly.
Ah, I have found the prisoner index.
Rungar, war crimes, cabinet 45, chamber S. Subjectric, mass murder, cabinet 43, chamber L.
Salieri, mind crimes, cabinet 9.
Chamber T, cabinet 9.
Commander, leave two Krags to guard this machine. You can bring Romana. Come, my dear, and meet the great Salieri.
Doctor, we've arrived. We're on Sharda.
Good. Now, you two stay here.
Why should we?
I'm not at liberty to explain. K-9, you can come along, but you're not to tangle with any Krags.
Affirmative, master.
Unless, of course, you have to tangle with any Krags.
Hurry. Skagra will be here already.
This is where your precious Time Lords used to put the criminals they simply wanted to forget about.
I've never even heard of it.
Evidently, you forget very thoroughly on Gallifrey. This way.
Well, here we are. My TARDIS must be in this direction.
But Skagra will have got in that direction. How do you know?
I heard footsteps. If I can get back to my TARDIS first, we can stop Skagra getting it back.
He'll have no escape.
But it is imperative we find him before he finds Seljevin.
Yes, but let's just exercise a little strategy, shall we?
Observe. The prisoners of Sharda. Each one in his own separate cryogenic cell.
Alive, but frozen. In perpetual imprisonment.
A very humane solution, don't you think?
Don't look at me. I'm not answerable for the Time Lords.
But you are, Madam President.
But...
Oh, I'm sorry.
Did you really think the information in this sphere didn't show me exactly who you and the Doctor truly are?
All right, Skagra. But I'm not responsible for the actions of previous administrations.
Oh, no matter. Time Lords will soon be irrelevant.
Krag, Commander.
My Lord.
Stay here until I call for you. The rest of you, follow me.
Now, we shall find Seljevin.
It's odd the way some days work out, isn't it?
I mean, there I was, just cycling down King's Parade.
Chris, there's something very odd about the Professor.
Oh, why single out the Professor?
Why have we been abandoned in here anyway?
One minute we're fighting those Krag things, the next, stay put.
I feel like a pet dog, but another pet dog.
I want to know what's going on out there.
Chris, you're not listening to me.
I just don't like getting left behind.
I mean, just because we come from Earth doesn't give everyone the right to be patronising towards us.
But, admittedly, all this stuff in here does make us look a bit primitive.
I haven't got the faintest idea how it all works.
I have.
You have?
At least I did have, for a few minutes.
What do you mean?
That's what I've been trying to tell you all along.
It's something that the Professor did to me.
To my mind.
Well done, K-9.
It is guarded by two Krags.
Oh, well, so much for strategy. All right, we'll do it your way.
Before we go, K-9.
Professor?
If Skagra tries to use the sphere on anyone, you must destroy it.
Affirmative.
I intend destroying it anyway. Come on, let's find Skagra and Romana.
At last. The man I have spent my life searching for.
The man who will reshape the entire universe.
Salyadin. Let us release him.
No, Skagra, stop!
Doctor!
Keep away from here!
Skagra, you must not press that button!
Commander, you and your fellow Krags persuade our uninvited guests to keep back, please!
You are too late, Doctor!
Salyadin is released!
Salyadin!
Who are you? Where is Salyadin?
Well, I should have thought that was obvious by now.
I escaped centuries ago.
Let me just get this right.
You say that he just... just walked into your mind?
Well, sort of.
It's as if he just barged in through the front door and started shuffling my thoughts about.
But the Doctor said that ability was unique to the guy Skagra's company.
And that he would come here to find.
Which would mean that Professor Kronotus is...
On your feet, Keatley!
Come on, let's see what's happening.
You're Salyadin?
Yes, I am, Doctor.
That's why I wanted no one to come here.
I wanted to live my life out in peace.
To forget the stupidities of my past.
To forget this hateful power.
I have suppressed it for years, except where it was necessary to cover my tracks.
Now go, Skagra.
Leave me in peace.
Forget this insanity.
No, Salyadin.
I have you here.
I have everything I need.
Do not force me to use my power on you, Skagra.
Canine, the sphere. Shoot it.
Sphere unassailable by my weaponry, Master.
Professor, look out!
No! No!
Keep away!
Excellent.
And now for you, Doctor.
Stay very, very still.
The sphere has taken what it wants from the Professor's mind, but it seems fond of you.
You've had one chance to take my mind, Skagra.
Why should I give you another?
You're right, Doctor.
Sphere, I want my army.
Doctor, I've just realized.
What is it?
It's the Kraks.
Skagra insisted on creating mindless ones because he wanted...
Because he's going to let the sphere put minds into their bodies.
Top of the class, both of you.
Sphere, now.
No, Skagra.
For heaven's sake, you can't give those brutes fragments of those minds.
Observe, Doctor.
That's just what I am doing.
Now, Doctor, you shall see the beginning of the universal mind.
